subject: Marketplace list-price rebate / reseller netback question
messages:
From: partners-ops@resellerco.com (ResellerCo Partner Ops)
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.hansen@acme.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace -- list-price rebate / joint netback ask

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Quick note from ResellerCo on behalf of Acme: they're trying to close a private-offer PO in the GCP marketplace but their procurement insists on a one-line reseller rebate off the invoice (so the ERP reflects a lower effective price).

The marketplace private-offer flow appears to require a list-price floor for catalog SKUs; Acme's procurement wants the rebate treated as a post-invoice credit (so their GL shows the reduced spend). That combination is creating a conflict with our standard pass-through expectations and the SKU list-price mapping.

Can Redwood:
- confirm whether a post-invoice rebate is acceptable for GCP private offers (we've attached the price_matrix.xlsx with SKUs and requested rebate % per SKU),
- provide a quick netback workback per SKU (post-rebate, marketplace fee, and reseller commission), and
- flag any platform or compliance constraints we should be aware of (tax handling, invoicing visibility, evidence for audits).

Timeline: Acme is asking for an official statement by EOD Thu PST to attach to their procurement packet. Can you advise feasibility and next steps?

Attachments: price_matrix.xlsx (requested rebate % per SKU)

Thanks,
--
ResellerCo Partner Ops
partners-ops@resellerco.com

-Tessa

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, partners-ops@resellerco.com
Cc: laura.hansen@acme.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace -- list-price rebate / joint netback ask

Good context — appreciate the attachment. Two quick product/ops notes from sales perspective:

- We usually avoid changing the marketplace "list price" on catalog SKUs because it breaks comparability and public listings. The common approach is a commit-based discount at time of offer creation combined with a reseller commission overlay that appears as a separate line (or credit) on settlement.
- If procurement insists on a post-invoice credit (rather than pre-offer discounted list), we need to be explicit on tax and settlement timing — that can alter the netback math.

I'll propose: provide a worked example for the top 3 SKUs showing both options (1) pre-offer list price discount and (2) post-invoice rebate credit. If Marcus can run both scenarios we can recommend the one that preserves marketplace rules and gives Acme the ledger they need.

Linking our internal private-offer playbook for reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/marketplace/private-offer-guidelines

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 16, 2027 at 9:12 AM partners-ops@resellerco.com wrote:
> Hi Tessa / Ben,
> 
> Quick note from ResellerCo on behalf of Acme: they're trying to close a private-offer PO in the GCP marketplace but their procurement insists on a one-line reseller rebate off the invoice (so the ERP reflects a lower effective price).
> 
> The marketplace private-offer flow appears to require a list-price floor for catalog SKUs; Acme's procurement wants the rebate treated as a post-invoice credit (so their GL shows the reduced spend). That combination is creating a conflict with our standard pass-through expectations and the SKU list-price mapping.

I ran the numbers for the top 3 SKUs in the attached revenue_workback.csv. Summary here (USD):

- SKU A (compute-heavy): list price $12,000, requested rebate 12% -> post-rebate $10,560; marketplace fee 4% -> settlement $10,137.6; proposed reseller commission 8% of list = $960 -> netback to Redwood $9,177.6.
- SKU B (ingest bundle): list price $4,000, requested rebate 10% -> post-rebate $3,600; marketplace fee 4% -> settlement $3,456; reseller commission 8% of list = $320 -> netback $3,136.
- SKU C (addon feature): list price $800, requested rebate 15% -> post-rebate $680; marketplace fee 4% -> settlement $652.8; reseller commission 8% of list = $64 -> netback $588.8.

Key finance notes:
- If the rebate is applied post-invoice (i.e., as a credit), our accounting treatment changes: invoiced revenue will still be at list but we must book contra-revenue for the rebate; margin recognition timing can be different and may require accrual adjustments.
- Tax treatment: in some jurisdictions rebates reduce taxable base only if processed as invoice-level credit. We should treat tax advice as out-of-scope for finance; recommend customer loop in their tax counsel.
- Marketplace fees are applied on settlement (post-rebate in most current marketplace implementations). Confirming with platform is required.

Recommendation: If Acme needs their ERP to show the lower effective spend, the cleanest path is a post-invoice credit (procurement-friendly) but that requires legal & accounting sign-off and explicit language in the private-offer terms. If speed matters, pre-offer discounted list price keeps accounting simpler but may not satisfy procurement visibility needs.

Attaching: revenue_workback.csv and a one-page sample statement we can provide to procurement if platform allows post-invoice credit (private_offer_terms_draft.pdf).

-Marcus
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
